title: Conventions registry
idSyntax: An id is a namespace, a colon and a value. The value is everything after the first colon and may itself hold colons, semicolons, slashes or an @. A receipt that holds a value under a field names the id of that field's namespace and that value.

groups.title: Natal receipt fields and time records

namespaces.name: zodiac
namespaces.title: Zodiac
namespaces.description: How longitudes are counted.

entries.title: Tropical zodiac
entries.definition: Longitudes counted from the equinox of the frame the position is given in. A natal receipt's positions are on the ecliptic and true equinox of date, so its zodiac counts from the true equinox of date.

entries.title: Sidereal zodiac
entries.definition: Longitudes counted from an ayanamsa's sidereal zero point: the longitude in the ecliptic of date less the true ayanamsa (true equinox) or the mean one (mean equinox). The receipt's ayanamsa id names which ayanamsa.

namespaces.name: ayanamsa
namespaces.title: Ayanamsa
namespaces.description: The offset between the tropical and a sidereal zodiac. A built-in ayanamsa carries its own citation; a caller's ayanamsa is held in the receipt's request.

entries.title: Lahiri (Chitrapaksha)
entries.definition: 23°15′00.658″ true at 1956-03-21 0h TT, with IAU 1976 precession, held at J2000.0 and carried on by the engine's precession.

sources.title: Indian Astronomical Ephemeris: 23°15′00.658″ true at 1956-03-21 0h TT (1989, p. 556)

entries.title: Fagan-Bradley
entries.definition: 24°02′31.36″ mean at B1950.0 (JD 2433282.42345905 TT), from the synetic vernal point at 335°57′28.64″, with Newcomb's precession.

entries.title: Krishnamurti (KP)
entries.definition: 22°21′50″ at 1900-01-01 0h TT (JD 2415020.5), with Newcomb's precession: a fit to Krishnamurti's own table.

sources.title: 22°21′50″ at 1900-01-01, fitted to KP Reader 1's table (Hand, Dawson)

entries.title: Raman
entries.definition: (year − 397) × 50⅓″: zero at J397.0 (JD 1866049.25 TT), growing by 50⅓″ a Julian year, as B. V. Raman gives the formula (1935).

sources.title: B. V. Raman, A Manual of Hindu Astrology (1935) §49

entries.title: Sri Yukteswar
entries.definition: 20°54′36″ at the March equinox of 1894 (JD 2412908.1244 TT), growing by 54″ a Julian year, as Sri Yukteswar gives it (1894).

sources.title: Sri Yukteswar, The Holy Science (1894), Introduction

entries.title: True Chitra (Spica at 180°)
entries.definition: Spica (α Vir) at 180°: the star's apparent geocentric longitude of date, from the Hipparcos new reduction, held at that sidereal longitude.

sources.title: F. van Leeuwen (2007), Validation of the new Hipparcos reduction, Astronomy & Astrophysics 474, 653-664

entries.title: True Revati (ζ Psc at 359°50′)
entries.definition: ζ Psc at 359°50′, held as for True Chitra.

sources.title: F. van Leeuwen (2007), Validation of the new Hipparcos reduction, Astronomy & Astrophysics 474, 653-664

entries.title: True Pushya (δ Cnc at 106°)
entries.definition: δ Cnc at 106°, held as for True Chitra.

sources.title: P. V. R. Narasimha Rao (2013); Hipparcos 2007 (I/311)
F. van Leeuwen (2007), Validation of the new Hipparcos reduction, Astronomy & Astrophysics 474, 653-664

entries.title: Galactic Center at 0° Sagittarius
entries.definition: Sgr A* at 240° (0° Sagittarius), from its ICRS radio position with Reid and Brunthaler's proper motion, treated as infinitely distant.

sources.title: Sgr A*: SIMBAD ICRS position; Reid & Brunthaler 2004
F. van Leeuwen (2007), Validation of the new Hipparcos reduction, Astronomy & Astrophysics 474, 653-664

entries.title: A caller's ayanamsa at an epoch
entries.definition: A mean ayanamsa the caller gives at an epoch, carried by the engine's precession, or held where the Newcomb or IAU 1976 precession puts it at J2000.0 when the caller names that model. The receipt's request holds the definition.

entries.title: A caller's linear ayanamsa
entries.definition: An ayanamsa the caller gives as a value at an epoch plus a fixed rate in arcseconds per Julian year, with no precession model. The receipt's request holds the definition.

namespaces.name: frame
namespaces.title: Frame
namespaces.description: The plane and equinox a position is given in. In an equatorial frame the longitude is right ascension, in degrees, and the latitude is declination.

entries.title: Ecliptic, true equinox of date
entries.definition: The ecliptic of date and the true equinox: IAU 2006 precession, the IAU 2006 mean obliquity and the IAU 2000B nutation in longitude. The frame of a natal chart's positions.

sources.title: N. Capitaine, P. T. Wallace and J. Chapront (2003), Expressions for IAU 2000 precession quantities, Astronomy & Astrophysics 412, 567-586
D. D. McCarthy and B. J. Luzum (2003), An abridged model of the precession-nutation of the celestial pole, Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy 85, 37-49

entries.title: Ecliptic, mean equinox of date
entries.definition: The ecliptic and mean equinox of date: the same rotation without the nutation.

sources.title: N. Capitaine, P. T. Wallace and J. Chapront (2003), Expressions for IAU 2000 precession quantities, Astronomy & Astrophysics 412, 567-586
D. D. McCarthy and B. J. Luzum (2003), An abridged model of the precession-nutation of the celestial pole, Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy 85, 37-49

entries.title: Ecliptic of J2000.0
entries.definition: The mean ecliptic and equinox of J2000.0: the mean equator and equinox of J2000.0 turned by the IAU 2006 obliquity of J2000.0, 84381.406″.

sources.title: N. Capitaine, P. T. Wallace and J. Chapront (2003), Expressions for IAU 2000 precession quantities, Astronomy & Astrophysics 412, 567-586
D. D. McCarthy and B. J. Luzum (2003), An abridged model of the precession-nutation of the celestial pole, Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy 85, 37-49

entries.title: Ecliptic on ICRS axes
entries.definition: The ICRS turned by 84381.406″ about its x axis.

sources.title: N. Capitaine, P. T. Wallace and J. Chapront (2003), Expressions for IAU 2000 precession quantities, Astronomy & Astrophysics 412, 567-586
D. D. McCarthy and B. J. Luzum (2003), An abridged model of the precession-nutation of the celestial pole, Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy 85, 37-49

entries.title: Equator, true equinox of date
entries.definition: The true equator and equinox of date: apparent right ascension and declination, with IAU 2006 precession and the IAU 2000B nutation, on the true obliquity.

sources.title: N. Capitaine, P. T. Wallace and J. Chapront (2003), Expressions for IAU 2000 precession quantities, Astronomy & Astrophysics 412, 567-586
D. D. McCarthy and B. J. Luzum (2003), An abridged model of the precession-nutation of the celestial pole, Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy 85, 37-49

entries.title: Equator, mean equinox of date
entries.definition: The mean equator and equinox of date: the precession alone.

sources.title: N. Capitaine, P. T. Wallace and J. Chapront (2003), Expressions for IAU 2000 precession quantities, Astronomy & Astrophysics 412, 567-586
D. D. McCarthy and B. J. Luzum (2003), An abridged model of the precession-nutation of the celestial pole, Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy 85, 37-49

entries.title: Equator of J2000.0
entries.definition: The mean equator and equinox of J2000.0, the axes astronomy-engine's precession starts from (EQJ).

sources.title: N. Capitaine, P. T. Wallace and J. Chapront (2003), Expressions for IAU 2000 precession quantities, Astronomy & Astrophysics 412, 567-586
D. D. McCarthy and B. J. Luzum (2003), An abridged model of the precession-nutation of the celestial pole, Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy 85, 37-49

entries.title: ICRS
entries.definition: The ICRS: the J2000.0 equator less the IAU 2000 frame bias.

sources.title: N. Capitaine, P. T. Wallace and J. Chapront (2003), Expressions for IAU 2000 precession quantities, Astronomy & Astrophysics 412, 567-586
D. D. McCarthy and B. J. Luzum (2003), An abridged model of the precession-nutation of the celestial pole, Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy 85, 37-49

namespaces.name: center
namespaces.title: Center
namespaces.description: The origin a position is seen from.

entries.title: Geocentric
entries.definition: Seen from the Earth's centre.

entries.title: Heliocentric
entries.definition: Seen from the Sun's centre.

entries.title: Barycentric
entries.definition: Seen from the solar-system barycentre, as astronomy-engine finds it from the Sun and the four giant planets.

entries.title: Topocentric
entries.definition: Seen from an observer on the Earth's surface, on astronomy-engine's ellipsoid and turned by the engine's Greenwich apparent sidereal time, with no polar motion.

namespaces.name: correction
namespaces.title: Correction
namespaces.description: Which corrections a position carries.

entries.title: Apparent
entries.definition: Light time and aberration: the observer is backdated with the target, which adds the observer's aberration to first order. No gravitational deflection.

entries.title: Astrometric
entries.definition: Light time only: the target when its light left, from where the observer is when it arrives.

entries.title: Geometric
entries.definition: Where the target is at the instant, from where the observer is at the instant.

entries.title: Not applicable
entries.definition: For the lunar nodes and Lilith, geocentric points of the Moon's orbit, where the three corrections give the same position.

namespaces.name: light-time
namespaces.title: Light time
namespaces.description: How the light time is solved.

entries.title: Newtonian light time
entries.definition: astronomy-engine's light-time solution, iterated until successive light times agree to 10⁻⁹ day.

namespaces.name: aberration
namespaces.title: Aberration
namespaces.description: How aberration is applied.

entries.title: Backdated observer
entries.definition: First-order aberration from backdating the observer with the target.

namespaces.name: deflection
namespaces.title: Deflection
namespaces.description: Whether gravitational light deflection is applied.

entries.title: No deflection
entries.definition: No gravitational deflection of light.

namespaces.name: moon
namespaces.title: Moon
namespaces.description: How the Moon's position is found.

entries.title: Lunar series at the instant
entries.definition: The engine's Moon: astronomy-engine's lunar series at the instant, without light time or aberration.

namespaces.name: precession
namespaces.title: Precession
namespaces.description: The precession model.

entries.title: IAU 2006 precession
entries.definition: The angles of Capitaine et al. (2003) as astronomy-engine applies them, without a frame bias; named in every frame for the lunar nodes and Lilith, which are found in the ecliptic of date.

sources.title: N. Capitaine, P. T. Wallace and J. Chapront (2003), Expressions for IAU 2000 precession quantities, Astronomy & Astrophysics 412, 567-586

namespaces.name: nutation
namespaces.title: Nutation
namespaces.description: The nutation model, in either receipt.

entries.title: IAU 2000B
entries.definition: The engine's IAU 2000B nutation (McCarthy and Luzum 2003): all 77 luni-solar terms and the two fixed planetary offsets.

sources.title: D. D. McCarthy and B. J. Luzum (2003), An abridged model of the precession-nutation of the celestial pole, Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy 85, 37-49

entries.title: IAU 2000B, with complementary terms
entries.definition: The engine's IAU 2000B series, all 77 luni-solar terms and the two fixed planetary offsets, with the two largest complementary terms in the equation of the equinoxes.

sources.title: D. D. McCarthy and B. J. Luzum (2003), An abridged model of the precession-nutation of the celestial pole, Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy 85, 37-49
G. Petit and B. Luzum (eds.), IERS Conventions (2010), IERS Technical Note 36

namespaces.name: obliquity
namespaces.title: Obliquity
namespaces.description: The obliquity of the ecliptic.

entries.title: IAU 2006 obliquity
entries.definition: The IAU 2006 mean obliquity, 84381.406″ at J2000.0, with the nutation in obliquity for a true-of-date frame; named in every frame for the lunar nodes and Lilith.

sources.title: N. Capitaine, P. T. Wallace and J. Chapront (2003), Expressions for IAU 2000 precession quantities, Astronomy & Astrophysics 412, 567-586

namespaces.name: frame-bias
namespaces.title: Frame bias
namespaces.description: The rotation between the ICRS and the J2000.0 equator.

entries.title: IAU 2000 frame bias
entries.definition: The IAU 2000 frame bias of the ICRS (IERS Conventions 2010, equation 5.21).

sources.title: G. Petit and B. Luzum (eds.), IERS Conventions (2010), IERS Technical Note 36

namespaces.name: barycentre
namespaces.title: Barycentre
namespaces.description: How the solar-system barycentre is found.

entries.title: Sun and giant planets
entries.definition: astronomy-engine's solar-system barycentre, from the Sun and the four giant planets, each weighted m / (m + M☉).

namespaces.name: observer
namespaces.title: Observer
namespaces.description: Where a topocentric observer stands.

entries.title: IERS 2003 ellipsoid, no polar motion
entries.definition: The topocentric observer's position and velocity on the IERS 2003 ellipsoid, without polar motion.

sources.title: G. Petit and B. Luzum (eds.), IERS Conventions (2010), IERS Technical Note 36

namespaces.name: node
namespaces.title: Lunar node
namespaces.description: Which lunar node.

entries.title: True (osculating) node
entries.definition: The node of the Moon's osculating orbit, from its geocentric state vector.

entries.title: Mean node
entries.definition: The Moon's mean node: IERS 2003's Ω plus the nutation in longitude.

sources.title: G. Petit and B. Luzum (eds.), IERS Conventions (2010), IERS Technical Note 36

namespaces.name: lilith
namespaces.title: Lilith
namespaces.description: Which Black Moon Lilith.

entries.title: Mean Lilith
entries.definition: Black Moon Lilith as the Moon's mean apogee.

namespaces.name: speed
namespaces.title: Speed
namespaces.description: How speeds are found, in either receipt.

entries.title: Analytic speeds
entries.definition: For geometric positions on fixed axes (the J2000.0 and ICRS frames) of every body but the Moon: astronomy-engine's velocities from its differentiated series (Pluto's from its integrator), turned into the frame.

entries.title: Central difference, ±0.001 day
entries.definition: The value at t + h less the value at t − h, over 2h, with h = 0.001 day: the method wherever speeds are not analytic.

entries.title: Central difference, ±0.25 day
entries.definition: Central difference with h = 0.25 day, for the true node, whose short-period motion would otherwise dominate.

entries.title: Degrees per day, ±0.001 day, nodes ±0.25 day
entries.definition: Speeds in degrees per day by central difference over ±0.001 day, and over ±0.25 day for the nodes.

entries.title: Degrees per day, ±0.25 day
entries.definition: Speeds in degrees per day by central difference over ±0.25 day.

namespaces.name: ephemeris
namespaces.title: Ephemeris
namespaces.description: The ephemeris, by name and version. A natal receipt names it in engine.ephemeris.

entries.title: astronomy-engine 2.1.19
entries.definition: astronomy-engine 2.1.19: truncated VSOP87 for the planets, a lunar series after Brown's theory as Montenbruck and Pfleger give it, and an integrated Pluto.

namespaces.name: deltat
namespaces.title: ΔT source
namespaces.description: Where a calc receipt's ΔT comes from. Not the natal receipt's deltaT convention, which is its own namespace.

entries.title: ΔT from the time basis
entries.definition: ΔT from the engine's time basis: iers-utc/1 from 1972-01-01 to the end of the IERS table, zodiacs-deltat/1 outside it; each instant's deltaT.model says which.

sources.title: @zodiacs/engine 1.0.0, docs/time.md, From an instant to UT1 and TT

entries.title: Pinned ΔT
entries.definition: The caller's ΔT value, pinned.

sources.title: @zodiacs/engine 1.0.0, docs/time.md, From an instant to UT1 and TT

namespaces.name: time
namespaces.title: Time basis
namespaces.description: How a calc receipt's instants become UT1 and TT.

entries.title: The engine's time basis
entries.definition: From 1972-01-01 to the end of the IERS UT1 table, TT from the leap seconds (UTC + (TAI − UTC) + 32.184 s) and UT1 from IERS UT1 − UTC; outside that span, the instant read as UT1 and TT from the ΔT model. The natal receipt names the same basis in its timeScale convention.

sources.title: @zodiacs/engine 1.0.0, docs/time.md, From an instant to UT1 and TT
IERS Bulletin C, leap seconds (TAI − UTC)

namespaces.name: house
namespaces.title: House system
namespaces.description: The house system. A natal receipt names the system asked for and the one used in houses.requested and houses.actual; the compute API takes the same names.

entries.title: Whole sign
entries.definition: Each sign is a house, the first the ascendant's.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

entries.title: Placidus
entries.definition: The semi-arcs of each degree divided in thirds. Undefined where |latitude| ≥ 90° − ε.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

entries.title: Porphyry
entries.definition: Each quadrant between the angles divided into three equal arcs of longitude.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

entries.title: Equal
entries.definition: 30° each from the ascendant.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

entries.title: Equal from the midheaven
entries.definition: 30° each, the 10th from the midheaven; the same at every latitude.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

entries.title: Vehlow
entries.definition: 30° each, with the ascendant in the middle of the first.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

entries.title: Koch
entries.definition: Ascendants at thirds of the midheaven degree's semi-arc. Undefined where |latitude| ≥ 90° − ε.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

entries.title: Regiomontanus
entries.definition: Circles through the horizon's north and south points, every 30° of the equator.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

entries.title: Campanus
entries.definition: Circles through the horizon's north and south points, every 30° of the prime vertical.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

entries.title: Topocentric (Polich-Page)
entries.definition: Regiomontanus's ascensions, with pole heights at one and two thirds of the latitude's tangent.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

entries.title: Alcabitius
entries.definition: The ascendant's semi-arcs divided in thirds on the equator, along hour circles.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

entries.title: Morinus
entries.definition: The equator every 30° from the midheaven's right ascension, carried to the ecliptic through its poles.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

entries.title: Meridian (axial rotation)
entries.definition: Right ascensions every 30° from the midheaven's; the 1st cusp is the equatorial ascendant.

sources.title: R. W. Holden, The Elements of House Division (L. N. Fowler, 1977)

namespaces.name: polar-fallback
namespaces.title: Polar fallback
namespaces.description: What the engine uses where a house system is undefined.

entries.title: Whole sign in polar regions
entries.definition: Whole-sign houses where Placidus or Koch is undefined, at |latitude| ≥ 90° − ε with ε the true obliquity of date; the chart also carries the polar-fallback flag.

namespaces.name: angles
namespaces.title: Angles
namespaces.description: How the ascendant and midheaven are found.

entries.title: Apparent sidereal time and true obliquity
entries.definition: The angles from the engine's Greenwich apparent sidereal time and the true obliquity of date.

entries.title: Apparent sidereal time and mean obliquity
entries.definition: The angles from Greenwich apparent sidereal time and the mean obliquity of date.

namespaces.name: sidereal-time
namespaces.title: Sidereal time
namespaces.description: How Greenwich apparent sidereal time is found.

entries.title: GAST from the Earth rotation angle
entries.definition: Greenwich apparent sidereal time from the Earth rotation angle, astronomy-engine's IAU 2006 polynomial, and the equation of the equinoxes: Δψ cos εA and the two largest IAU 2000 complementary terms.

sources.title: N. Capitaine, P. T. Wallace and J. Chapront (2003), Expressions for IAU 2000 precession quantities, Astronomy & Astrophysics 412, 567-586
G. Petit and B. Luzum (eds.), IERS Conventions (2010), IERS Technical Note 36

namespaces.name: aspects
namespaces.title: Aspects
namespaces.description: Which aspects a chart lists and how.

entries.title: Major aspects
entries.definition: The chart's major aspects, as a calc chart lists them.

entries.title: Major aspects, applying by orb rate
entries.definition: The major aspects among the Sun, the Moon and the eight planets, not the nodes, each applying or separating by the instantaneous rate of change of its orb.

entries.title: Major aspects
entries.definition: The major aspects among the Sun, the Moon and the eight planets, not the nodes.

namespaces.name: search
namespaces.title: Search
namespaces.description: How a calc event search finds crossings.

entries.title: Scan and bisect
entries.definition: The engine's crossing search: every instant in (from, to] the body sits on the longitude, bracketed by a scan in steps and bisected, within a budget of evaluations.

namespaces.name: calendar
namespaces.title: Calendar
namespaces.description: The calendar dates are written in.

entries.title: Proleptic Gregorian
entries.definition: Dates in the Gregorian calendar, extended before its adoption in 1582.

sources.title: ISO 8601-1:2019, Date and time: Representations for information interchange, Part 1 (the proleptic Gregorian calendar)

namespaces.name: deltaT
namespaces.title: ΔT
namespaces.description: What a natal receipt's ΔT is and where it is given. Not the calc receipt's deltat source.

entries.title: TT − UT1, in the result
entries.definition: ΔT is TT − UT1, and the result gives its value; the time basis decides how the instant is read.

entries.title: TT − UT1, the instant read as UT1
entries.definition: ΔT is TT − UT1, the instant is read as UT1, and the result gives the value.

namespaces.name: localTime
namespaces.title: Local time
namespaces.description: How a local wall time becomes UTC.

entries.title: Shipped tzdb before 1970, Intl from 1970
entries.definition: Local times before 1970 resolved on the tzdb history the engine ships, from 1970 on the host's Intl, and the gap, fold and local-mean-time flags taken from the transition record.

namespaces.name: longitudeUnit
namespaces.title: Longitude unit
namespaces.description: The unit and range of longitudes.

entries.title: Degrees in [0, 360)
entries.definition: Longitudes in degrees, from 0 up to but not including 360.

namespaces.name: moonNodes
namespaces.title: Moon nodes
namespaces.description: Which lunar nodes a natal chart gives.

entries.title: Instantaneous orbit plane
entries.definition: The nodes of the plane of the Moon's instantaneous geocentric orbit: the true (osculating) nodes.

namespaces.name: moonPosition
namespaces.title: Moon position
namespaces.description: How a natal chart's Moon is found.

entries.title: astronomy-engine GeoMoon, ecliptic of date
entries.definition: astronomy-engine's geocentric lunar series (GeoMoon), turned to the ecliptic of date by the engine's precession and nutation, without light time or aberration.

entries.title: astronomy-engine EclipticGeoMoon, uncorrected
entries.definition: astronomy-engine's ecliptic geocentric Moon (EclipticGeoMoon), without light time or aberration.

entries.title: astronomy-engine EclipticGeoMoon
entries.definition: astronomy-engine's ecliptic geocentric Moon (EclipticGeoMoon).

namespaces.name: planetPositions
namespaces.title: Planet positions
namespaces.description: How a natal chart's planets are found.

entries.title: Geocentric, light time and aberration, ecliptic of date
entries.definition: Geocentric positions corrected for light time and aberration but not for gravitational deflection, on the ecliptic of date.

entries.title: Apparent geocentric, ecliptic of date
entries.definition: Apparent geocentric positions on the ecliptic of date.

namespaces.name: timeScale
namespaces.title: Time scale
namespaces.description: How a natal chart's instant becomes UT1 and TT, and where the basis is recorded.

entries.title: The engine's time basis, in the result
entries.definition: From 1972-01-01 to the end of the IERS UT1 table, TT from the leap seconds and UT1 from IERS UT1 − UTC; otherwise the instant read as UT1 and TT from the ΔT model; the basis recorded in the result's timeScale.

sources.title: @zodiacs/engine 1.0.0, docs/time.md, From an instant to UT1 and TT
IERS Bulletin C, leap seconds (TAI − UTC)

namespaces.name: house-absence
namespaces.title: House absence
namespaces.description: Why a natal chart has no houses.

entries.title: Unknown birth time
entries.definition: The birth time is unknown, so the chart has no angles or houses.

entries.title: No birthplace
entries.definition: No birthplace was given, so the chart has no angles or houses.

namespaces.name: flag
namespaces.title: Chart flag
namespaces.description: A condition a natal chart reports, in the receipt's input and result flags.

entries.title: Clock gap
entries.definition: The local time fell in a gap of any cause, such as a change to summer time, and was moved forward.

entries.title: Clock fold
entries.definition: The local time fell in a fold of any cause and could be read twice; the earlier reading was taken.

entries.title: Local mean time
entries.definition: A local mean time clock read the wall time.

entries.title: No birth time
entries.definition: The birth time is unknown; the chart has no angles or houses.

entries.title: Polar fallback
entries.definition: Placidus or Koch was asked for where it is undefined, and the chart uses whole-sign houses.

entries.title: Outside the reference span
entries.definition: The instant lies outside 1800-01-01 to 2200-01-01, the span over which positions were compared with an independent ephemeris (the engine's REFERENCE_SPAN); the chart is still computed.

namespaces.name: reference
namespaces.title: Reference instant
namespaces.description: Which instant a natal chart is cast for.

entries.title: The supplied instant
entries.definition: The chart is cast for the instant given.

entries.title: Noon UTC
entries.definition: An untimed chart cast for 12:00 UTC on the date.

entries.title: Local noon
entries.definition: An untimed chart cast for 12:00 local time on the date.

namespaces.name: time-scale
namespaces.title: Instant time scale
namespaces.description: The scale of a receipt's instant.

entries.title: UTC
entries.definition: Coordinated Universal Time.

sources.title: @zodiacs/engine 1.0.0, docs/time.md, From an instant to UT1 and TT

entries.title: UT1
entries.definition: Universal Time, the Earth's rotation angle as a time.

sources.title: @zodiacs/engine 1.0.0, docs/time.md, From an instant to UT1 and TT

entries.title: TT
entries.definition: Terrestrial Time: TAI + 32.184 s.

sources.title: @zodiacs/engine 1.0.0, docs/time.md, From an instant to UT1 and TT

namespaces.name: time-basis
namespaces.title: Time basis
namespaces.description: Which branch of the time basis an instant took.

entries.title: NASA JPL Horizons (DE441) apparent geocentric ecliptic positions, carried into the IAU 2006/2000A true ecliptic and equinox of date
entries.definition: The independent arbiter of L1 (Positions) vectors. Source: NASA JPL Horizons API 1.2 (https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api), fetched 2026-09-22: ephemeris DE441 for every target, with Mars to Pluto as their system barycentres (NAIF 4 to 9); EOP file eop.260922.p261219 (data 1962-01-20 to 2026-09-22, predictions to 2026-12-18). One request per target: EPHEM_TYPE OBSERVER, CENTER 500@399 (the geocentre), QUANTITIES 31 (observer ecliptic longitude and latitude of date of the apparent position: light-time, gravitational deflection by the Sun, stellar aberration), APPARENT AIRLESS, TIME_TYPE TT, TLIST_TYPE JD with the 24 jd_tt values to 8 decimals, ANG_FORMAT DEG, EXTRA_PREC YES, CSV_FORMAT YES. The responses are kept verbatim in sources/horizons-24/, byte for byte as committed in the zodiacs.org site repository (ZodiacsOfficial/site, docs/platform/evidence/engine-beyond-swiss/corpora/horizons-24/, commit 3f31ba17), together with Horizons's body-centre files for Mars to Pluto (NAIF 499 to 999, from the satellite solutions mar099, jup365_merged, sat441l, ura184_merged, nep098_merged, plu060_merged), fetched the same way and used only for the body-centre measurement in the uncertainty. Plus the frame conversion: Horizons labels this frame IAU76/80 ecliptic-of-date, and the eopJpl model of it, with its per-instant celestial-pole offsets, is the horizons-frame study in the same repository (docs/platform/evidence/engine-beyond-swiss/horizons-frame/: decompose.py, results.json), the offsets copied into sources/horizons-24/frame-offsets.json.

entries.title: IANA tzdb 2025c with backzone, compiled by zic 2025c
entries.definition: The independent arbiter of L3 (Time and calendars) vectors. Source: IANA time zone database release 2025c: https://data.iana.org/time-zones/releases/tzdata2025c.tar.gz (sha256 4aa79e4effee53fc4029ffe5f6ebe97937282ebcdf386d5d2da91ce84142f957) and https://data.iana.org/time-zones/releases/tzcode2025c.tar.gz (sha256 697ebe6625444aef5080f58e49d03424bbb52e08bf483d3ddb5acf10cbd15740), both OpenPGP-signed by Paul Eggert (key 7E37 92A9 D8AC F7D6 33BC 1588 ED97 E90E 62AA 7E34; signatures checked 2026-09-28). The data are the Makefile's `make PACKRATDATA=backzone PACKRATLIST=zone.tab` build: backzone's pre-1970 history for the zone.tab zones that the main data merge into links. Why backzone: a birth chart needs the local time in force where and when the birth happened, often before 1970, and tzdb's default build does not keep that history for these zones; it makes each of them a link to another zone whose clocks have agreed with it since 1970, so the zone answers with the other zone's history (Africa/Banjul at 1880-12-31T12:00:00 gets Abidjan's local mean time, -968 s, instead of its own, -3996 s). The maintainers' caveat applies: the Makefile of tzdata 2025c offers backzone as 'out-of-scope and often-wrong data', and its theory.html says the file 'is less reliable and does not necessarily follow database guidelines'. zic and zdump are built from the same release's tzcode.
